datasets.title: Belarus: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/blr-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values are derived from VIIRS satellite observations at 10-day temporal resolution. Anomalies are calculated at each grid cell by computing the deviation from a long-term mean baseline spanning 2012 to the most recent complete year. The resulting raster datasets are provided as GeoTIFF files for annual periods, enabling temporal monitoring of vegetation health as a proxy indicator for agricultural drought impacts.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides FAPAR biophysical measurements from VIIRS satellite imagery. FAPAR anomalies are calculated as deviations from long-term mean baseline (2012 onwards) to indicate vegetation stress and agricultural drought conditions.
